text:
alyssa: Quick sync — need a compact GA acceptance checklist for the next release. Focus: SLAs, docs, oncall, monitoring, pricing readiness. Can we align scope today?

brian: I can do runtime / perf SLA items. proposing: 99.9% availability for hosted API, 100ms p50 + 350ms p95 on our standard 4k token profile for US regions. Those are ambitious but reachable with dedicated pools.

maria: For monitoring, we need explicit alert thresholds and runbook links. Suggest: page when error rate > 0.5% for 5m or request latency p95 > 500ms for 10m. Also add an SLO burn alert at 75% monthly error budget.

jeff: Sales needs a clear SLA table for pricing and entitlements. Tiering: Free / Standard / Enterprise. Enterprise gets SLA + dedicated capacity + 24x7 oncall. Can we lock what counts as "incident" vs "degraded"?

alyssa: Good point. Let's define incident = customer-facing outage causing >1% of customers to fail requests or regional outage. Degraded = sustained latency/error increase but < incident threshold. We should include fallback behaviors (auto-failover to compatible model variant).

katie: Docs: Quickstart, API reference, migration guide, and an "SLA & Support" page. Owners: katie -> quickstart + API PR, maria -> monitoring/runbooks, brian -> perf tuning notes + model fallback docs.

brian: For model fallbacks, I'll add a small snippet for routing policy config: ```
routing_policy:
  primary: gpt-like-v2
  fallback: gpt-quantized-v2
  max_latency_ms: 500
```

maria: Runbook skeleton (short): 1) Detect alert 2) Triage (region/model) 3) Switch routing policy -> fallback 4) Notify customer comms. I'll put the actual playbook in confluence and link from docs.

jeff: Pricing readiness: we need final per-token numbers and note about discounts for reserved capacity. Also callout for overage handling and credits policy. Marketing wants a simple one-pager.

alyssa: Decision needed on scope: do we ship early support for private (VPC) in GA or mark it as "enterprise beta"? Private has longer security review and entitlements. Recommend GA = hosted + dedicated; private as GA-early enterprise feature.

brian: I agree. Private requires on-prem packaging and extra testing. Better to exclude from GA to avoid scope creep.

katie: That helps docs scope. We'll include a clear "Private (VPC/on-prem) - enterprise beta" note on the product page with prerequisites and expected timelines.

maria: Oncall rota: product release week needs overlap from eng-sre and runtime team. Proposed schedule: eng-sre primary first 72h, runtime secondary; then rotate to standard oncall. Need headcount confirmation.

deploy-bot: Deployment snapshot: canary at 10% in us-west, feature-flagged fallback enabled, alerting hooks wired to #incidents. Commit: 7a2f9d.

alyssa: Action items: 1) brian: finalize SLA numbers + perf test results by EOD tomorrow. 2) maria: publish runbook + alert thresholds by EOD. 3) katie: land Quickstart + API reference draft and pricing one-pager. 4) jeff: finalize enterprise SLA wording and discounts. I'll consolidate into the GA acceptance checklist and share for sign-off.

jeff: noted, I'll push the SLA wording and a sample contract clause for escalations.

brian: I'll also include a short appendix with recommended quantization options and expected cost deltas for Optimize team.

maria: If anyone needs me to simulate alerts for runbook validation, ping me and I'll spin a fire drill.

alyssa: Thanks all — if we can hit the deliverables, we can target the GA cut next Tuesday. Post any blockers here. :thumbsup:
